_comment: TODO: Populate with labeled ground-truth bugs for the seeded_bugs/ samples. Each entry should describe the file, the seeded bug's location/type, and whether it is actually a bug.

_schema_example.id: string - unique id matching a file in seeded_bugs/
_schema_example.is_bug: boolean - whether this sample actually contains a bug
_schema_example.bug_type: string - e.g. 'off-by-one', 'null-deref', 'sql-injection', or null if not a bug
_schema_example.line: integer|null - line number of the bug, if applicable
_schema_example.description: string - short human description of the bug

bugs.description: Off-by-one: `end = start + page_size + 1` includes one extra item, so each page overlaps the next page by one item.
Off-by-one: `range(len(values) - window)` stops one iteration short, so the moving average silently drops the last valid window.
Off-by-one: `range(0, len(items) - 1, batch_size)` can exclude a valid starting index at `len(items) - 1`, silently dropping the last chunk of items.
Wrong comparison operator: uses `>` instead of `<=`, so batteries above the low-battery threshold are reported as low and batteries at or below it are not.
Wrong comparison operator: uses `<=` instead of `>=`, so orders under the free-shipping threshold ship free while orders that actually qualify are charged.
Wrong comparison operator: the 'C' branch uses `>` instead of `>=`, so a score of exactly 70 incorrectly falls through to grade 'D'.
Incorrect boundary condition: loop uses `low < high` instead of `low <= high`, so the search misses the target when it is the last remaining candidate.
Incorrect boundary condition: uses `length <= MIN_LENGTH` instead of `length < MIN_LENGTH`, so a password exactly at the minimum length is incorrectly rejected.
Bad state handling: `cart=[]` is a mutable default argument, so the same list is reused and accumulates items across unrelated calls to `add_item`.
Bad state handling: `reset_on_success` is a no-op (`pass`), so `attempts` is never reset and a tracker that already succeeded still reports exhausted retries afterward.
SQL injection: the query string is built with `%` string formatting on `username` instead of a parameterized query, so a crafted username can alter the SQL statement.
Command injection: `hostname` is concatenated directly into a shell command passed to `os.system`, so a crafted hostname (e.g. containing `;`) can execute arbitrary shell commands.
Hardcoded secret: `SECRET_KEY` is a literal string committed in source rather than loaded from an environment variable or secret manager, exposing the signing key to anyone with source access.
Insecure deserialization: `pickle.loads` is called on `raw_cookie_value`, which comes from a client-controlled cookie; a crafted pickle payload can execute arbitrary code.
Weak cryptography: passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5, which is fast to brute-force and unsuitable for password storage; should use a slow, salted algorithm like bcrypt or scrypt.
Bare except clause: `except:` catches every exception (including KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit), silently masking bugs unrelated to int parsing.
Shadowed builtin: the local variable `dict` shadows the builtin `dict` type within the function, which is confusing and error-prone if the constructor is needed later in scope.
Unused variable: `tax` is computed but never added to the total or included in the receipt output, so the computation is dead code and the receipt silently omits tax.

Singleton comparison: `user["active"] == True` should be a plain truthy check; as written it silently excludes active users whose `active` field is truthy but not the literal `True` (e.g. a non-boolean truthy value).

Inconsistent return statements: there is no `else`/default branch, so an unrecognized `customer_tier` causes the function to implicitly return `None`, which later crashes `apply_discount`'s arithmetic.
